analysis: The patch is confined to SSDPrefixCache.evictOldestEntry (head ~1772-1777; base 1772-1786). It replaces the inline loop over index.oldestEntries() with a call to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:), whose closure still calls retireIndexedEntries([url]) on the same fileURL derived from config.root and the HMAC tag. The hasSafeRoot guard is retained, and the stats increment now happens only when freed > 0. The supplied excerpts do not include SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest or the retireIndexedEntries/performIndexedRemoval internals (the head text shown ends at line 656). So I could not verify two points from the supplied evidence. First, that the helper preserves the old semantics: skip valid-but-undeletable victims, stop on retired.externalChange, and return the freed bytes of one entry. Second, that the ownsEvictionRoot and removalLock checks remain on the path. Because the closure still routes through retireIndexedEntries, which in the base code is the path guarded by performIndexedRemoval and ownsEvictionRoot, I identified no concrete regression. A behavioral drift in the helper could affect TB-007/T-041 at-rest TTL/LRU purge bounds and disk budget enforcement (availability of the box-wide budget if the helper stops after one failed victim). Integration should confirm the SSDOwnedEntryRetirement implementation (a new or changed file outside this batch) handles the externalChange early return, skips undeletable victims, and does not unlink paths without the safe-root and epoch ownership checks. No unsafe-path, key, or exposure changes were visible in this diff. The scanOnDisk, settleDurableDonation and lookup code in the units is unchanged context.
